item.text: {"text":"TREC’s 2025 Product Recommendation task provides a directly relevant diagnostic taxonomy: functional substitutes; related but neither substitute nor complement; full complements; complements with unknown compatibility; explicitly incompatible complements; unrelated; and unable to assess. Its examples distinguish shared function from actual compatibility: different camera systems can be conceptual substitutes, while a Samsung phone and iPhone case are incompatible complements. This supports separating semantic association, supported complementarity, explicit conflict, and insufficient evidence. These are product-pair judgments, not evidence of individual purchase need. [Official task definitions](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html).\n\nPractical adaptation, inferred from these definitions: attach title/description evidence spans to every compatibility claim, then compare scores for closely related compatible and explicitly incompatible candidates. Such pairs offer diagnostic hard negatives without equating semantic similarity with usefulness. Missing model identifiers, connectors, dimensions, or prerequisite evidence should produce an unknown state; absence from history does not establish nonownership. A substitute resembling a historical purchase supports only “possible redundant purchase,” since replacement, gifting, collecting, or replenishment remain unobserved. Keep unknown cases out of confidently labeled negative sampling; use supported conflicts to investigate targeted sampling or pairwise loss changes, validating any benefit with the unchanged macro HR@10 evaluator. The literature also recognizes asymmetric complementarity and coexistence of substitute/complement relations, reinforcing caution about simple similarity rules. [2024 complementary-recommendation survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135)."}
